status: Ought Not to Pass pursuant to Joint Rule 310, 2011-05-17
key_provisions: Proposed to encourage computer data center development; not a moratorium.

status: Ought Not to Pass pursuant to Joint Rule 310, 2018-03-22
key_provisions: Proposed sales tax refund/exemption structure for computer data center development; not a moratorium.

status: Ought Not to Pass pursuant to Joint Rule 310, 2011-03-15
key_provisions: Proposed to bring a "green data center" to Maine; not a moratorium.

sponsors: Rep. Melanie Sachs; original bill page also identifies Rep. Drew Gattine on adopted amendment H-1051
status: Passed both chambers (House enactment vote 83-66, 2026-04-08); vetoed by Gov. Janet Mills 2026-04-24; House override attempt failed 72-65 (92 needed for 2/3) on 2026-04-29; Veto Sustained, 2026-04-29
key_provisions: Would have prohibited any municipality, state agency, or quasi-independent state entity from accepting applications or issuing permits, certificates, or approvals for development, construction, or operation of a data center with a load of 20 MW or more until 2027-11-01. Would have created the Maine Data Center Coordination Council to study ratepayer, grid reliability, environmental, host-community, data-sharing, impact fee, demand response, and community benefit agreement issues, with report due 2027-02-01.

bill: LD 713 / HP 452, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2026, c. 768
status: Signed by Governor 2026-04-23, Public Law 2026 c. 768
key_provisions: Excludes data centers beginning operations on or after 2026-08-01 from the Business Equipment Tax Exemption and Dirigo Business Incentives Program. Defines "data center" in Title 36 and requires the Department of Economic and Community Development to study financial incentives that data centers may benefit from, with report due 2026-11-04.

bill: LD 912 / SP 402, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2025, c. 85
status: Emergency enacted and signed by Governor 2025-05-23, Public Law 2025 c. 85
key_provisions: Amended Title 35-A definition of transmission and distribution utility. A private-distribution exception for a northern Maine commercial or industrial site does not apply if more than 25% of the entity's nameplate capacity serves data centers on that site.
